news.title: Football: Soccer-I preferred my old life, says Cape Verde World Cup hero Vozinha
news.lede: Sept 28 (Reuters) - Vozinha kept ⁠clean sheets against eventual champions Spain and Saudi Arabia with ⁠his exceptional goalkeeping to help Cape Verde reach the ‌World Cup round of 32 this year, but the 40-year-old feels powerless to cope with the intense attention that fame has brought his way. Cape Verde, a collection ​of islands near Africa's west coast with ⁠apopulation of some 500,000, ⁠surprisingly reached the knockout stage in their first appearance at the global ⁠tournament ‌before losing 3-2 to Argentina. news.title: Parma agree deal with Gilardino as Italy World Cup winner set to return as coach
news.lede: Alberto Gilardino is set to return to Parma as a coach, having reached an agreement with the Ducali to replace Carlos Cuesta. Parma and Cuesta parted ways by mutual consent on Sunday, and today the former Arsenal assistant coach returned to the training centre one last time to say goodbye to the team and empty his locker. Gilardino, an ex-Parma and Italy striker, has already agreed to take over at the Stadio Tardini and will sign his contract later today, according to Sky Sport, TMW and Tuttosport. Gilardino scored 56 goals in 116 Parma games between 2002 and 2005, after which he joined Serie A giants Milan.

news.title: ‘I’ve lost my peace and tranquillity’: Vozinha on the price of World Cup fame
news.lede: Six months ago, Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha was largely unknown outside football circles. His life revolved around the small Portuguese city of Chaves, where he played in the country’s second tier. Then came the FIFA World Cup 2026, and everything changed. The 40-year-old goalkeeper became one of the tournament’s unexpected stars after Cape Verde’s historic campaign.

news.title: Vozinha pays the price of his World Cup fame: "I preferred my life before, I have lost my peace"'
news.lede: Vozinha, Cape Verde's goalkeeper who at 40 became a football star at the 2026 World Cup, admits in an interview with "The Observer" that "I preferred my life before fame, I have lost my peace and quiet".' "I no longer have privacy, or at least I have much less than before. Now I go out, I go to a restaurant, and there is always someone who wants to take a photo with me or ask me for an autograph. Or, even worse, someone is filming me.

news.title: Terim: Italy have ‘significant potential’ but no identity
news.lede: Former Fiorentina and Milan coach Fatih Terim insists Italy must ‘rediscover identity and competitiveness’ and backs the Turkish FA’s decision to confirm Vincenzo Montella in charge despite a disappointing World Cup exit.Italy visit Vincenzo Montella’s Turkiye in the second match of the 2026-27 Nations League group phase tonight. Both sides lost their opening games against Belgium and France, respectively.“. It’s an extremely important match, because both Italy and Turkiye need a win,” Terim told Gazzetta. (Photo by Marco Rosi/Getty Images)%“We know how difficult a period your national team is going through, but this is also a good opportunity for Turkiye to restart after the World Cup.”

news.title: Vozinha: From World Cup hero to a fight for his future
news.lede: Vozinha enjoyed a remarkable 2026 World Cup with Cape Verde, but the veteran goalkeeper has endured a difficult few weeks since the tournament. At 40, he became one of the competition’s surprise stars, helping the Blue Sharks reach the Round of 16 on their historic debut. His standout display against Spain, which ended in a 0-0 draw, and several spectacular saves attracted attention from clubs around the world. After considering moves to Inter Miami and RS Berkane, Vozinha eventually joined Colo-Colo in Chile on a short-term deal.

news.title: Again, Spain dominate, beat DPR Korea to win FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup 2026
news.lede: September 28, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports 0. Spain’s remarkable domination of international football has continued after the country’s U20 women’s national team defeated defending champions DPR Korea on penalties to win the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. The final in Łódź ended goalless after 120 minutes, with neither side able to break the deadlock during regulation time or extra time. Spain eventually prevailed 4-3 in the penalty shootout, with goalkeeper Laia López emerging as the hero after making two crucial saves to secure the trophy for La Rojita.

news.title: I preferred my life before fame - I've lost my peace and tranquillity, says World Cup hero Vozinha
news.lede: VOZINHA claims that he preferred life before he became a World Cup viral sensation. The veteran goalkeeper, 40, shot to stardom as Cape Verde earned a 0-0 draw with eventual winners Spain in the group stage. His social media following shot from 56,000 to over one million during the match. The stopper, then a free agent after leaving Portuguese second tier side Chaves, subsequently landed a big move to Chilean giants Colo-Colo.
